summary.one_liner: Eidolon is an open-source SDK for building agent-based services and deploying them over a built-in HTTP server.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Eidolon as an SDK for developers to build and deploy agent-based services. It states that agents are exposed as services with a built-in HTTP server, so no separate deployment setup is described. It says agents have well-defined interfaces and that other agents can use them as tools, with tools generated dynamically from the OpenAPI JSON schema the agent services define. It also says components such as LLMs, RAG implementations, and tools are modular and can be swapped out or replaced with custom ones. The README does not list specific LLM providers, languages, or detailed API usage; it points to an external website and Quickstart Guide for those.
use_cases: deploying AI agents as HTTP services
swapping LLMs or RAG components in an agent
generating tools from OpenAPI schemas for agents
how_to_run: See the Quickstart Guide linked from the project website (no install commands in the README)
stack: unknown: README does not name languages or runtimes
notable: Agents are deployed as services with a built-in HTTP server
Agent-to-agent calls use tools generated from each service's OpenAPI JSON schema
Modular components that can be swapped (LLMs, RAG, tools) to avoid vendor lock-in
Uses an all-contributors specification for credits
caveats: README is brief and gives no install or run commands; it defers to the website and Quickstart Guide
Languages, supported LLM providers, and license details are not stated in the README
